parsed.reason: The message states facts (Sunnyside Splash Pad on Friday for $14, Beaches Rec Centre opening September 3, Maya's 18-month vaccine visit overdue) with no attribution showing Hale looked anything up. There is no first-person verb of finding or checking in the lead sentence or anywhere that presents these as results of work Hale already did. Instead, the message opens with "Great news!" which functions as a greeting/product introduction, and the facts land flat without any "I found," "I checked," or similar attribution. The closing rhetorical flourish ("There is honestly so much going on around you this week that I could barely fit it all in") and the offer question undermine rather than establish that these facts came from a look Hale took. The facts read as trivia a stranger might send, indistinguishable from information the parent already knew.
